A two-player derivative of Whist where players spend the first half of the game playing tricks to improve their hand, then the second half playing out that hand.

Only half the deck is dealt, and the game begins with additional series of 13 non-scoring tricks in which each trick determines how the top two cards of the draw deck are dealt to the players, the winner of each trick getting the top card (which is always revealed before the trick is played) and the losing player getting the second (hidden) card.

The game is a quick to learn, easy to arrange, and fast-playing introduction to trick-taking games and serves as a good first step to learning to play Whist or Bridge for players unfamiliar with trick-taking.

[Rating: 3/10] Meh, 2p trick taking doesn't excite me.  The 1st phase drafting in theory sounds interesting, but it's very luck based if you get a good card draw when you lose a trick.  2nd phase plays out kind of predictably since you know exactly what cards your opponent has.

[Rating: 5/10] This is the game I'd naturally play when I'm somewhere with two players and just a pack of cards to keep us amused

[Rating: 5/10] We were looking for a quick two player card game and stumbled on this in a card game rule book.  A fine way to pass a few minutes and the card drafting strategy is more in depth than we first gave it credit for (particularly if you score all tricks taken rather than just the last 13)

[Rating: 5/10] An interesting little 2 player standard trick taker. I swear the free computer program cheats, funny how it is always lacking the right card and the right time!    So its a 2 phase little game. In the 1st phase you play to win tricks but only to win either the top face up card from deck OR if it sucks you try to lose the trick hoping that the card underneath is better and if your lucky Trump. This continues until the deck runs out and then you have 13 cards still left (1st phase everytime you play one you gain one, tricks are not kept and worth nothing).   2nd phase you play for keeps, trying 

[Rating: 5/10] Two-player trick-taking game with two stages, the first of which is building your hand and the second of which is playing for points. There is luck of the draw, but it's pretty interesting how you can employ low cards while drafting, and leech off good cards in the process. Card counting is a huge deal, though: you are playing the last thirteen tricks with open hands if anyone's been paying attention.

[Rating: 5/10] A mostly enjoyable 2 player trick taking game design, but I've had too many hands where luck absolutely determined everything that happened and that can start to add up after a while.

[Rating: 5/10] Overview: The game is split up into two. In the first half, players are building up their hand by playing tricks. The trick winner gets the open card while the trick loser gets the hidden cards. After 13 tricks, the second half of the game starts in which one needs to win as many tricks as possible.  What I like: - Build up a more powerful hand in the first part of the game.  What I dislike:  - Maybe a tad too straightforward and boring.

[Rating: 5.5/10] [Poker Game] {Card, couple; trick-taking}  German Whist is a genuine 2p trick-taking.  It is a tactical game - players have to plan carefully in the first stage to collect cards for the second stage.  There is some luck involved and players can take risk to draw the face-down card, rather than the face-up cards in order to have a better card.  Players will good card counting certainly has advantage because each player shall know the hand of the other play when the first stage finishes, and thus can act accordingly. [Rating: 5.7/10] Nice game, but I prefer to play with only 32 cards (Piquet deck) instead of the full deck.

[Rating: 6/10] Although I mostly use it to introduce others to the concepts found in WYSIWYG, it's pretty rare for me to turn down a hand or two of German Whist. I mean, come on. It takes about six minutes to play.

[Rating: 6/10] Based on 10 plays. + One of the actually interesting games you can play with a traditional card deck.  Since 2009, updated Dec 2011.
